title: The legal fallout of the commercial surrogacy ban
p1:
A law can stop a market overnight, but it cannot erase the demand behind it.

The ban on commercial surrogacy changed more than just contracts — it reshaped the legal rights and responsibilities of everyone involved.
p2:
Many assume that banning commercial surrogacy simply protects women from exploitation. But the legal reality is more complex.

After the ban, only altruistic surrogacy is allowed in India, meaning the surrogate cannot receive monetary compensation beyond certain permitted expenses. This created new questions around consent, medical risks, and access for intended parents.
p3:
The biggest legal challenge is balancing protection with choice.

A regulation meant to prevent exploitation must also consider whether genuine arrangements, especially those involving infertility struggles, have enough legal clarity and support.

The lesson is simple: when a law changes an industry, it must address not only the problem it targets but also the consequences it creates.
conclusion: Do you think banning commercial surrogacy protects vulnerable women, or does it create new legal challenges that need attention?
